$comment: FORMAT-v3 §2. Section IDs and section types are independent namespaces, and two section types may legally occur more than once. Both properties are invisible in a Core-only pack, where IDs 1-6 equal their types and every type appears once, so an implementation can conflate them and pass every other check in this packet.

both_overlays.why: Carries an ANN-7 expansion and an ANN-8 SPLADE overlay: two sections of type 13. A reader applying the singleton rule to every V3-defined type rejects this artifact. Verified to discriminate: adding 13 to the Core reader's known-type set makes it fail with 'duplicate singleton section type 13'.

sections.name: term_overlay
sections.note: expansion; id equals type by coincidence

sections.name: term_overlay
sections.note: splade; type 14 is retired, so a reader resolving id 14 as a type finds nothing

sections.name: lexical_terms
sections.note: type 17 is passage_records, so conflating id and type yields a real section of the wrong kind

core_only.why: The contrast case. The same off-by-one exists here -- id 17 is type 16, id 18 is type 17 -- so ID/type conflation is not fat-pack-specific. What the fat pack adds is one type occurring twice.

$adapter_limitation: The adapter contract exposes tokenize, search, open and verify-receipt, none of which report section ids or types, so the runner asserts only that both artifacts open. The `sections` tables above are the normative expectation an implementer should check against their own parser; they are documentation the runner cannot currently execute. Making them executable requires a fifth adapter verb and is deliberately not done here.
